text: GET /posts returns an array of exactly 100 post objects.
GET /posts/1 returns a single post object containing id, title, body, and userId fields.
GET /posts?userId=1 filters and returns only posts belonging to the specified user.
GET /posts/1/comments returns all comments associated with post 1.
GET /comments?postId=1 returns the same results as GET /posts/1/comments.
POST /posts with a JSON body and Content-Type: application/json returns the submitted fields plus a generated id of 101.
POST /posts does not actually persist data to the server.
PUT /posts/1 with a full JSON body returns the submitted fields for the specified post.
PUT /posts/1 does not actually update data on the server.
PATCH /posts/1 with a partial JSON body returns the existing post with only the submitted fields changed.
PATCH /posts/1 does not actually modify data on the server.
DELETE /posts/1 is accepted by the API.
DELETE /posts/1 does not actually remove data from the server.
The API supports both http and https protocols.
GET /albums/1/photos returns all photos belonging to album 1.
GET /users/1/albums returns all albums belonging to user 1.
GET /users/1/todos returns all todos belonging to user 1.
GET /users/1/posts returns all posts belonging to user 1.
The API contains 10 users, 100 albums, 200 todos, 500 comments, and 5000 photos in total.
